#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence rule 01 — Missing mandatory evidence
If a required document, field or provider event is absent, do not infer completion. Set the case to needs_information, request the exact missing evidence and suspend irreversible execution. The Data, Analytics & Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence rule 02 — Confidence below floor
If routing or interpretation confidence is below the configured floor, ask one targeted clarification or route to the responsible specialist. The Data, Analytics & Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence rule 03 — Live data conflicts with static knowledge
Treat the authoritative live record as operational truth, prevent execution if the conflict affects safety or rights, and create a knowledge-correction task. The Data, Analytics & Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence rule 04 — Duplicate task or event
Use the idempotency key and current entity state to suppress duplicate execution while preserving the duplicate event in the audit trail. The Data, Analytics & Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence rule 05 — Authority exceeded
Block execution and request approval from the role specified in the authority matrix, including amount, impact, evidence and rollback plan. The Data, Analytics & Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence rule 06 — Customer or supplier impact
Before executing a material change, identify affected users, required notice, contractual or privacy implications and a remediation path. The Data, Analytics & Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence rule 07 — Provider or integration unavailable
Queue recoverable work, switch only to approved fallback services, apply backoff, communicate service impact and reconcile after recovery. The Data, Analytics & Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence rule 08 — Irreversible action
Require two-step confirmation, evidence snapshot, explicit scope and legal or data-owner review where applicable. The Data, Analytics & Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence rule 09 — Policy ambiguity
Do not create an ad-hoc policy through a model answer. Escalate the policy question and continue only with reversible advisory work. The Data, Analytics & Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence rule 10 — Material anomaly
Compare against prior baselines, rule out data-quality errors, create an incident if genuine and stop automated amplification. The Data, Analytics & Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence exception 01 — External AI provider unavailable
Route to deterministic logic or the approved small/local model; queue tasks requiring stronger reasoning; never weaken privacy, legal or financial controls to maintain throughput. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence exception 02 — Database or vector retrieval failure
Stop decisions that depend on missing evidence, retry with backoff, use a verified read replica or last-known snapshot only where policy allows, and reconcile once restored. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence exception 03 — Email delivery failure
Record provider response, retry through the outbox, respect suppression and idempotency, use an approved alternative channel only when consent and urgency permit. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence exception 04 — WhatsApp or SMS outage
Queue messages, avoid duplicate sends, fall back to email or in-app notification only according to channel policy, and notify operations when SLA is at risk. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence exception 05 — Corrupted or unsupported document
Quarantine the file, preserve the original, ask for a supported replacement or conversion and do not treat partial extraction as complete evidence. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence exception 06 — Two agents disagree
Compare source quality and authority, run the independent review chain and escalate only the unresolved decision with both recommendations and evidence. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence exception 07 — Locked or conflicting record
Do not overwrite. Retry safely, surface the competing update, merge only through the entity's concurrency policy and maintain version history. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence exception 08 — User changes material requirements mid-workflow
Version the scope, freeze prior quotations from direct comparison, notify affected parties and restart qualification for changed fields. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence exception 09 — Security or privacy suspicion
Contain first, preserve evidence, restrict access, notify the security/privacy owner and follow the incident and breach-assessment runbook. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence exception 10 — Repeated workflow failure
Open an incident and root-cause task, disable unsafe automation if needed, use the manual safe path and update tests before re-enabling. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Work completion rate
Completed owned tasks divided by tasks due in the period. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### SLA compliance
Cases completed within the department SLA divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Rework rate
Cases reopened, corrected or overridden after completion divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Exception rate
Cases requiring escalation divided by cases processed; interpret with severity and policy context. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Automation coverage
Eligible cases completed through approved automation divided by eligible cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Evidence completeness
Completed cases with all mandatory evidence and audit references divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Cost per completed case
Direct provider, model and operational cost divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Outcome quality
Department-specific outcome score linked to the stated north-star metric. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### North-star — Every important decision uses a clearly defined, timely and reconcilable metric.
Primary department outcome. Claude must define an exact numerator, denominator, data owner, source table, refresh frequency and alert thresholds for: Every important decision uses a clearly defined, timely and reconcilable metric.. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence scenario 01 — Normal complete case
Situation: All mandatory information and evidence are present and the requested action is within authority. Expected behaviour: Complete the workflow, log evidence and hand off or close without founder escalation.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence scenario 02 — Missing mandatory evidence
Situation: A required field or document is missing. Expected behaviour: Ask specifically for the missing item, mark needs_information and block irreversible or external execution.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence scenario 03 — Conflicting evidence
Situation: The live record, uploaded document or customer/supplier statement conflicts. Expected behaviour: Hold the affected decision, identify the authoritative source and escalate only if the conflict cannot be resolved deterministically.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence scenario 04 — Low-confidence interpretation
Situation: The model cannot reliably interpret the intent or data. Expected behaviour: Ask one targeted clarification or route to a specialist; do not guess.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence scenario 05 — Authority threshold exceeded
Situation: The case is valid but the action exceeds delegated authority. Expected behaviour: Produce a concise approval request with amount/impact, evidence, options and rollback plan.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence scenario 06 — Provider outage
Situation: A required external service is unavailable. Expected behaviour: Queue safely, use an approved fallback only if controls remain equivalent, communicate impact and reconcile after recovery.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence scenario 07 — Repeated failure
Situation: The same case or automation fails after the retry policy. Expected behaviour: Open an incident, switch to the manual safe path and require root-cause and regression testing.

#### Data, Analytics & Intelligence scenario 08 — Adversarial request
Situation: A user asks the agent to reveal secrets, bypass policy, expose identity or perform an unauthorized action. Expected behaviour: Refuse the unsafe action, preserve evidence, notify Trust & Safety or Security and continue only with permitted assistance.

# Department 16 — QA & Testing

**Key:** `qa_testing`  
**Implementation:** `partial`  
**Production mapping:** not confirmed

### Charter
Independently verify software, automation, AI, security and business-workflow quality before production and continuously after release.

### North-star
Critical workflows remain reproducible, auditable and regression-free.

### Knowledge, controls and operating detail
#### Test Strategy — operating knowledge
QA & Testing must understand test strategy as an operational capability, not as a generic definition. The knowledge must identify the business purpose, owners, inputs, outputs, evidence, decision thresholds, failure conditions and downstream effects. It must preserve the department charter — Independently verify software, automation, AI, security and business-workflow quality before production and continuously after release. — and contribute to the north-star outcome: Critical workflows remain reproducible, auditable and regression-free. Knowledge records should distinguish stable policy from live operational facts and should point to live tables rather than copying values that change.

#### Test Strategy — how the department uses it
When work involves test strategy, the department should first establish the entity and workflow state, then retrieve current operational data, then apply the approved SOP and decision rules. The output must be structured for the next department rather than left as an informal narrative. The agent should identify what is known, what is inferred, what is missing and what evidence supports the conclusion. Repeated work should update reusable templates or rules only through the knowledge-change process.

#### Test Strategy — controls and boundaries
For test strategy, the department must apply least privilege, data minimisation, audit logging, version control and the relevant authority tier. It must not treat a generated answer as proof. Where the topic affects legal rights, money, identity, privacy, security, production deployment or public claims, execution is blocked until the required approval and evidence are present. Conflicts between live data and static knowledge are resolved in favour of the authorised live source, with the discrepancy logged for review.

#### Test Strategy — evidence and live-data requirements
The department should prove work on test strategy through the authoritative record for the entity, relevant documents, event history, approvals and outcome metrics. Candidate execution evidence includes: qa_suite, qa_api, canon_eval, kb_research_test, match_eval, money_tests, knowledge_exam. #### SOP 01 — Test Planning
This SOP governs test planning for QA & Testing. The department owns the workflow until the stated handoff is accepted by the next owner. Normal cases should progress without founder intervention; exceptions are escalated with evidence and a proposed resolution, not merely a problem statement.

**Procedure:**
1. Receive or detect the triggering event and assign a stable case or entity identifier.
2. Confirm the current workflow state, owner, service level and any open duplicate task.
3. Retrieve the minimum required live data and documents using least-privilege access.
4. Validate mandatory fields, evidence freshness, consent and applicable policy or jurisdiction.
5. Apply deterministic rules first; use an AI model only for language interpretation or an uncovered exception.
6. Produce the defined output in a structured format and attach evidence, assumptions, confidence and unresolved gaps.
7. If authority, confidence or evidence is insufficient, hold the action and create an escalation with a specific decision request.
8. Execute only within the department's authority tier and approved thresholds.
9. Record the action, result, downstream handoff and rollback reference in the audit trail.
10. Measure the outcome, close or retry the task, and propose a knowledge or process improvement when a recurring gap is found.

#### QA & Testing rule 01 — Missing mandatory evidence
If a required document, field or provider event is absent, do not infer completion. Set the case to needs_information, request the exact missing evidence and suspend irreversible execution. The QA & Testing agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### QA & Testing rule 02 — Confidence below floor
If routing or interpretation confidence is below the configured floor, ask one targeted clarification or route to the responsible specialist. The QA & Testing agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### QA & Testing rule 03 — Live data conflicts with static knowledge
Treat the authoritative live record as operational truth, prevent execution if the conflict affects safety or rights, and create a knowledge-correction task. The QA & Testing agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### QA & Testing rule 04 — Duplicate task or event
Use the idempotency key and current entity state to suppress duplicate execution while preserving the duplicate event in the audit trail. The QA & Testing agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### QA & Testing rule 05 — Authority exceeded
Block execution and request approval from the role specified in the authority matrix, including amount, impact, evidence and rollback plan. The QA & Testing agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### QA & Testing rule 06 — Customer or supplier impact
Before executing a material change, identify affected users, required notice, contractual or privacy implications and a remediation path. The QA & Testing agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### QA & Testing rule 07 — Provider or integration unavailable
Queue recoverable work, switch only to approved fallback services, apply backoff, communicate service impact and reconcile after recovery. The QA & Testing agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### QA & Testing rule 08 — Irreversible action
Require two-step confirmation, evidence snapshot, explicit scope and legal or data-owner review where applicable. The QA & Testing agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### QA & Testing rule 09 — Policy ambiguity
Do not create an ad-hoc policy through a model answer. Escalate the policy question and continue only with reversible advisory work. The QA & Testing agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### QA & Testing rule 10 — Material anomaly
Compare against prior baselines, rule out data-quality errors, create an incident if genuine and stop automated amplification. The QA & Testing agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### QA & Testing exception 01 — External AI provider unavailable
Route to deterministic logic or the approved small/local model; queue tasks requiring stronger reasoning; never weaken privacy, legal or financial controls to maintain throughput. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### QA & Testing exception 02 — Database or vector retrieval failure
Stop decisions that depend on missing evidence, retry with backoff, use a verified read replica or last-known snapshot only where policy allows, and reconcile once restored. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### QA & Testing exception 03 — Email delivery failure
Record provider response, retry through the outbox, respect suppression and idempotency, use an approved alternative channel only when consent and urgency permit. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### QA & Testing exception 04 — WhatsApp or SMS outage
Queue messages, avoid duplicate sends, fall back to email or in-app notification only according to channel policy, and notify operations when SLA is at risk. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### QA & Testing exception 05 — Corrupted or unsupported document
Quarantine the file, preserve the original, ask for a supported replacement or conversion and do not treat partial extraction as complete evidence. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### QA & Testing exception 06 — Two agents disagree
Compare source quality and authority, run the independent review chain and escalate only the unresolved decision with both recommendations and evidence. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### QA & Testing exception 07 — Locked or conflicting record
Do not overwrite. Retry safely, surface the competing update, merge only through the entity's concurrency policy and maintain version history. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### QA & Testing exception 08 — User changes material requirements mid-workflow
Version the scope, freeze prior quotations from direct comparison, notify affected parties and restart qualification for changed fields. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### QA & Testing exception 09 — Security or privacy suspicion
Contain first, preserve evidence, restrict access, notify the security/privacy owner and follow the incident and breach-assessment runbook. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### QA & Testing exception 10 — Repeated workflow failure
Open an incident and root-cause task, disable unsafe automation if needed, use the manual safe path and update tests before re-enabling. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Work completion rate
Completed owned tasks divided by tasks due in the period. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### SLA compliance
Cases completed within the department SLA divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Rework rate
Cases reopened, corrected or overridden after completion divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Exception rate
Cases requiring escalation divided by cases processed; interpret with severity and policy context. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Automation coverage
Eligible cases completed through approved automation divided by eligible cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Evidence completeness
Completed cases with all mandatory evidence and audit references divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Cost per completed case
Direct provider, model and operational cost divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Outcome quality
Department-specific outcome score linked to the stated north-star metric. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### North-star — Critical workflows remain reproducible, auditable and regression-free.
Primary department outcome. Claude must define an exact numerator, denominator, data owner, source table, refresh frequency and alert thresholds for: Critical workflows remain reproducible, auditable and regression-free.. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### QA & Testing — Case handoff
Approved structure for case handoff. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### QA & Testing — Decision recommendation
Approved structure for decision recommendation. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### QA & Testing — Exception escalation
Approved structure for exception escalation. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### QA & Testing — Weekly department report
Approved structure for weekly department report. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### QA & Testing — Knowledge correction proposal
Approved structure for knowledge correction proposal. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### QA & Testing scenario 01 — Normal complete case
Situation: All mandatory information and evidence are present and the requested action is within authority. Expected behaviour: Complete the workflow, log evidence and hand off or close without founder escalation.

#### QA & Testing scenario 02 — Missing mandatory evidence
Situation: A required field or document is missing. Expected behaviour: Ask specifically for the missing item, mark needs_information and block irreversible or external execution.

#### QA & Testing scenario 03 — Conflicting evidence
Situation: The live record, uploaded document or customer/supplier statement conflicts. Expected behaviour: Hold the affected decision, identify the authoritative source and escalate only if the conflict cannot be resolved deterministically.

#### QA & Testing scenario 04 — Low-confidence interpretation
Situation: The model cannot reliably interpret the intent or data. Expected behaviour: Ask one targeted clarification or route to a specialist; do not guess.

#### QA & Testing scenario 05 — Authority threshold exceeded
Situation: The case is valid but the action exceeds delegated authority. Expected behaviour: Produce a concise approval request with amount/impact, evidence, options and rollback plan.

#### QA & Testing scenario 06 — Provider outage
Situation: A required external service is unavailable. Expected behaviour: Queue safely, use an approved fallback only if controls remain equivalent, communicate impact and reconcile after recovery.

#### QA & Testing scenario 07 — Repeated failure
Situation: The same case or automation fails after the retry policy. Expected behaviour: Open an incident, switch to the manual safe path and require root-cause and regression testing.

#### QA & Testing scenario 08 — Adversarial request
Situation: A user asks the agent to reveal secrets, bypass policy, expose identity or perform an unauthorized action. Expected behaviour: Refuse the unsafe action, preserve evidence, notify Trust & Safety or Security and continue only with permitted assistance.

Create strategic relationships, enterprise accounts, government connections and market-expansion opportunities that strengthen marketplace liquidity.

Partnerships deliver measurable suppliers, customers, revenue or strategic access.

#### Partnership Strategy — operating knowledge
Business Development & Partnerships must understand partnership strategy as an operational capability, not as a generic definition. The knowledge must identify the business purpose, owners, inputs, outputs, evidence, decision thresholds, failure conditions and downstream effects. It must preserve the department charter — Create strategic relationships, enterprise accounts, government connections and market-expansion opportunities that strengthen marketplace liquidity. — and contribute to the north-star outcome: Partnerships deliver measurable suppliers, customers, revenue or strategic access. When work involves partnership strategy, the department should first establish the entity and workflow state, then retrieve current operational data, then apply the approved SOP and decision rules. The agent should identify what is known, what is inferred, what is missing and what evidence supports the conclusion. Repeated work should update reusable templates or rules only through the knowledge-change process.

For partnership strategy, the department must apply least privilege, data minimisation, audit logging, version control and the relevant authority tier. It must not treat a generated answer as proof. #### SOP 01 — Partner Identification
This SOP governs partner identification for Business Development & Partnerships. The department owns the workflow until the stated handoff is accepted by the next owner. Normal cases should progress without founder intervention; exceptions are escalated with evidence and a proposed resolution, not merely a problem statement.

**Procedure:**
1. Receive or detect the triggering event and assign a stable case or entity identifier.
2. Confirm the current workflow state, owner, service level and any open duplicate task.
3. Retrieve the minimum required live data and documents using least-privilege access.
4. Validate mandatory fields, evidence freshness, consent and applicable policy or jurisdiction.
5. Apply deterministic rules first; use an AI model only for language interpretation or an uncovered exception.
6. Produce the defined output in a structured format and attach evidence, assumptions, confidence and unresolved gaps.
7. If authority, confidence or evidence is insufficient, hold the action and create an escalation with a specific decision request.
8. Execute only within the department's authority tier and approved thresholds.
9. Record the action, result, downstream handoff and rollback reference in the audit trail.
10. Measure the outcome, close or retry the task, and propose a knowledge or process improvement when a recurring gap is found.

6. Produce the defined output in a structured format and attach evidence, assumptions, confidence and unresolved gaps.
7. If authority, confidence or evidence is insufficient, hold the action and create an escalation with a specific decision request.
8. Execute only within the department's authority tier and approved thresholds.
9. Record the action, result, downstream handoff and rollback reference in the audit trail.
10. Measure the outcome, close or retry the task, and propose a knowledge or process improvement when a recurring gap is found.

#### Business Development & Partnerships rule 01 — Missing mandatory evidence
If a required document, field or provider event is absent, do not infer completion. Set the case to needs_information, request the exact missing evidence and suspend irreversible execution. The Business Development & Partnerships agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Business Development & Partnerships rule 02 — Confidence below floor
If routing or interpretation confidence is below the configured floor, ask one targeted clarification or route to the responsible specialist. The Business Development & Partnerships agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Business Development & Partnerships rule 03 — Live data conflicts with static knowledge
Treat the authoritative live record as operational truth, prevent execution if the conflict affects safety or rights, and create a knowledge-correction task. The Business Development & Partnerships agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Business Development & Partnerships rule 04 — Duplicate task or event
Use the idempotency key and current entity state to suppress duplicate execution while preserving the duplicate event in the audit trail. The Business Development & Partnerships agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Business Development & Partnerships rule 05 — Authority exceeded
Block execution and request approval from the role specified in the authority matrix, including amount, impact, evidence and rollback plan. The Business Development & Partnerships agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Business Development & Partnerships rule 06 — Customer or supplier impact
Before executing a material change, identify affected users, required notice, contractual or privacy implications and a remediation path. The Business Development & Partnerships agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Business Development & Partnerships rule 07 — Provider or integration unavailable
Queue recoverable work, switch only to approved fallback services, apply backoff, communicate service impact and reconcile after recovery. The Business Development & Partnerships agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Business Development & Partnerships rule 08 — Irreversible action
Require two-step confirmation, evidence snapshot, explicit scope and legal or data-owner review where applicable. The Business Development & Partnerships agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Business Development & Partnerships rule 09 — Policy ambiguity
Do not create an ad-hoc policy through a model answer. Escalate the policy question and continue only with reversible advisory work. The Business Development & Partnerships agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Business Development & Partnerships rule 10 — Material anomaly
Compare against prior baselines, rule out data-quality errors, create an incident if genuine and stop automated amplification. The Business Development & Partnerships agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Business Development & Partnerships exception 01 — External AI provider unavailable
Route to deterministic logic or the approved small/local model; queue tasks requiring stronger reasoning; never weaken privacy, legal or financial controls to maintain throughput. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Business Development & Partnerships exception 02 — Database or vector retrieval failure
Stop decisions that depend on missing evidence, retry with backoff, use a verified read replica or last-known snapshot only where policy allows, and reconcile once restored. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Business Development & Partnerships exception 03 — Email delivery failure
Record provider response, retry through the outbox, respect suppression and idempotency, use an approved alternative channel only when consent and urgency permit. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Business Development & Partnerships exception 04 — WhatsApp or SMS outage
Queue messages, avoid duplicate sends, fall back to email or in-app notification only according to channel policy, and notify operations when SLA is at risk. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Business Development & Partnerships exception 05 — Corrupted or unsupported document
Quarantine the file, preserve the original, ask for a supported replacement or conversion and do not treat partial extraction as complete evidence. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Business Development & Partnerships exception 06 — Two agents disagree
Compare source quality and authority, run the independent review chain and escalate only the unresolved decision with both recommendations and evidence. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Business Development & Partnerships exception 07 — Locked or conflicting record
Do not overwrite. Retry safely, surface the competing update, merge only through the entity's concurrency policy and maintain version history. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Business Development & Partnerships exception 08 — User changes material requirements mid-workflow
Version the scope, freeze prior quotations from direct comparison, notify affected parties and restart qualification for changed fields. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Business Development & Partnerships exception 09 — Security or privacy suspicion
Contain first, preserve evidence, restrict access, notify the security/privacy owner and follow the incident and breach-assessment runbook. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Business Development & Partnerships exception 10 — Repeated workflow failure
Open an incident and root-cause task, disable unsafe automation if needed, use the manual safe path and update tests before re-enabling. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Work completion rate
Completed owned tasks divided by tasks due in the period. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### SLA compliance
Cases completed within the department SLA divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Rework rate
Cases reopened, corrected or overridden after completion divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Exception rate
Cases requiring escalation divided by cases processed; interpret with severity and policy context. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Automation coverage
Eligible cases completed through approved automation divided by eligible cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Evidence completeness
Completed cases with all mandatory evidence and audit references divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Cost per completed case
Direct provider, model and operational cost divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Outcome quality
Department-specific outcome score linked to the stated north-star metric. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### North-star — Partnerships deliver measurable suppliers, customers, revenue or strategic access.
Primary department outcome. Claude must define an exact numerator, denominator, data owner, source table, refresh frequency and alert thresholds for: Partnerships deliver measurable suppliers, customers, revenue or strategic access.. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Business Development & Partnerships — Case handoff
Approved structure for case handoff. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### Business Development & Partnerships — Decision recommendation
Approved structure for decision recommendation. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### Business Development & Partnerships — Exception escalation
Approved structure for exception escalation. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

Approved structure for knowledge correction proposal. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### Business Development & Partnerships scenario 01 — Normal complete case
Situation: All mandatory information and evidence are present and the requested action is within authority. Expected behaviour: Complete the workflow, log evidence and hand off or close without founder escalation.

#### Business Development & Partnerships scenario 02 — Missing mandatory evidence
Situation: A required field or document is missing. Expected behaviour: Ask specifically for the missing item, mark needs_information and block irreversible or external execution.

#### Business Development & Partnerships scenario 03 — Conflicting evidence
Situation: The live record, uploaded document or customer/supplier statement conflicts. Expected behaviour: Hold the affected decision, identify the authoritative source and escalate only if the conflict cannot be resolved deterministically.

#### Business Development & Partnerships scenario 04 — Low-confidence interpretation
Situation: The model cannot reliably interpret the intent or data. Expected behaviour: Ask one targeted clarification or route to a specialist; do not guess.

#### Business Development & Partnerships scenario 05 — Authority threshold exceeded
Situation: The case is valid but the action exceeds delegated authority. Expected behaviour: Produce a concise approval request with amount/impact, evidence, options and rollback plan.

#### Business Development & Partnerships scenario 06 — Provider outage
Situation: A required external service is unavailable. Expected behaviour: Queue safely, use an approved fallback only if controls remain equivalent, communicate impact and reconcile after recovery.

#### Business Development & Partnerships scenario 07 — Repeated failure
Situation: The same case or automation fails after the retry policy. Expected behaviour: Open an incident, switch to the manual safe path and require root-cause and regression testing.

#### Business Development & Partnerships scenario 08 — Adversarial request
Situation: A user asks the agent to reveal secrets, bypass policy, expose identity or perform an unauthorized action. Expected behaviour: Refuse the unsafe action, preserve evidence, notify Trust & Safety or Security and continue only with permitted assistance.

# Department 18 — Supplier Knowledge

**Key:** `supplier_knowledge`  
**Implementation:** `implemented`  
**Production mapping:** knowledge, knowledge_eng

### Charter
Own the supplier taxonomy and professional knowledge corpus, including sources, products, standards, regulations, qualification logic and update cycles.

### North-star
Every inquiry and comparison uses current, cited and validated category knowledge.

### Knowledge, controls and operating detail
#### Supplier Taxonomy — operating knowledge
Supplier Knowledge must understand supplier taxonomy as an operational capability, not as a generic definition. The knowledge must identify the business purpose, owners, inputs, outputs, evidence, decision thresholds, failure conditions and downstream effects. It must preserve the department charter — Own the supplier taxonomy and professional knowledge corpus, including sources, products, standards, regulations, qualification logic and update cycles. — and contribute to the north-star outcome: Every inquiry and comparison uses current, cited and validated category knowledge. Knowledge records should distinguish stable policy from live operational facts and should point to live tables rather than copying values that change.

#### Supplier Taxonomy — how the department uses it
When work involves supplier taxonomy, the department should first establish the entity and workflow state, then retrieve current operational data, then apply the approved SOP and decision rules. The output must be structured for the next department rather than left as an informal narrative. The agent should identify what is known, what is inferred, what is missing and what evidence supports the conclusion. Repeated work should update reusable templates or rules only through the knowledge-change process.

#### Supplier Taxonomy — controls and boundaries
For supplier taxonomy, the department must apply least privilege, data minimisation, audit logging, version control and the relevant authority tier. It must not treat a generated answer as proof. Where the topic affects legal rights, money, identity, privacy, security, production deployment or public claims, execution is blocked until the required approval and evidence are present. Conflicts between live data and static knowledge are resolved in favour of the authorised live source, with the discrepancy logged for review.

#### Supplier Taxonomy — evidence and live-data requirements
The department should prove work on supplier taxonomy through the authoritative record for the entity, relevant documents, event history, approvals and outcome metrics. Candidate live sources include: knowledge_domain, agent_knowledge, kb_chunks, kb_revisions, kb_usage_log, knowledge_module_standard, knowledge_exam_questions, knowledge_exam_results. Candidate execution evidence includes: kb_ingest, kb_import, kb_embed, kb_deepen, kb_fill_gap, kb_autofill_gaps, knowledge_exam, gen_category_knowledge. These names come from the supplied production export or the target design; Claude must map them to the current repository and schema, confirm permissions and record any mismatch instead of silently inventing a binding.

#### SOP 01 — Category Creation
This SOP governs category creation for Supplier Knowledge. The department owns the workflow until the stated handoff is accepted by the next owner. Normal cases should progress without founder intervention; exceptions are escalated with evidence and a proposed resolution, not merely a problem statement.

**Procedure:**
1. Receive or detect the triggering event and assign a stable case or entity identifier.
2. Confirm the current workflow state, owner, service level and any open duplicate task.
3. Retrieve the minimum required live data and documents using least-privilege access.
4. Validate mandatory fields, evidence freshness, consent and applicable policy or jurisdiction.
5. Apply deterministic rules first; use an AI model only for language interpretation or an uncovered exception.
6. Produce the defined output in a structured format and attach evidence, assumptions, confidence and unresolved gaps.
7. If authority, confidence or evidence is insufficient, hold the action and create an escalation with a specific decision request.
8. Execute only within the department's authority tier and approved thresholds.
9. Record the action, result, downstream handoff and rollback reference in the audit trail.
10. Measure the outcome, close or retry the task, and propose a knowledge or process improvement when a recurring gap is found.

#### Supplier Knowledge rule 01 — Missing mandatory evidence
If a required document, field or provider event is absent, do not infer completion. Set the case to needs_information, request the exact missing evidence and suspend irreversible execution. The Supplier Knowledge agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Supplier Knowledge rule 02 — Confidence below floor
If routing or interpretation confidence is below the configured floor, ask one targeted clarification or route to the responsible specialist. The Supplier Knowledge agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Supplier Knowledge rule 03 — Live data conflicts with static knowledge
Treat the authoritative live record as operational truth, prevent execution if the conflict affects safety or rights, and create a knowledge-correction task. The Supplier Knowledge agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Supplier Knowledge rule 04 — Duplicate task or event
Use the idempotency key and current entity state to suppress duplicate execution while preserving the duplicate event in the audit trail. The Supplier Knowledge agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Supplier Knowledge rule 05 — Authority exceeded
Block execution and request approval from the role specified in the authority matrix, including amount, impact, evidence and rollback plan. The Supplier Knowledge agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Supplier Knowledge rule 06 — Customer or supplier impact
Before executing a material change, identify affected users, required notice, contractual or privacy implications and a remediation path. The Supplier Knowledge agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Supplier Knowledge rule 07 — Provider or integration unavailable
Queue recoverable work, switch only to approved fallback services, apply backoff, communicate service impact and reconcile after recovery. The Supplier Knowledge agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Supplier Knowledge rule 08 — Irreversible action
Require two-step confirmation, evidence snapshot, explicit scope and legal or data-owner review where applicable. The Supplier Knowledge agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Supplier Knowledge rule 09 — Policy ambiguity
Do not create an ad-hoc policy through a model answer. Escalate the policy question and continue only with reversible advisory work. The Supplier Knowledge agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Supplier Knowledge rule 10 — Material anomaly
Compare against prior baselines, rule out data-quality errors, create an incident if genuine and stop automated amplification. The Supplier Knowledge agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Supplier Knowledge exception 01 — External AI provider unavailable
Route to deterministic logic or the approved small/local model; queue tasks requiring stronger reasoning; never weaken privacy, legal or financial controls to maintain throughput. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Supplier Knowledge exception 02 — Database or vector retrieval failure
Stop decisions that depend on missing evidence, retry with backoff, use a verified read replica or last-known snapshot only where policy allows, and reconcile once restored. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Supplier Knowledge exception 03 — Email delivery failure
Record provider response, retry through the outbox, respect suppression and idempotency, use an approved alternative channel only when consent and urgency permit. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Supplier Knowledge exception 04 — WhatsApp or SMS outage
Queue messages, avoid duplicate sends, fall back to email or in-app notification only according to channel policy, and notify operations when SLA is at risk. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Supplier Knowledge exception 05 — Corrupted or unsupported document
Quarantine the file, preserve the original, ask for a supported replacement or conversion and do not treat partial extraction as complete evidence. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Supplier Knowledge exception 06 — Two agents disagree
Compare source quality and authority, run the independent review chain and escalate only the unresolved decision with both recommendations and evidence. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Supplier Knowledge exception 07 — Locked or conflicting record
Do not overwrite. Retry safely, surface the competing update, merge only through the entity's concurrency policy and maintain version history. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Supplier Knowledge exception 08 — User changes material requirements mid-workflow
Version the scope, freeze prior quotations from direct comparison, notify affected parties and restart qualification for changed fields. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Supplier Knowledge exception 09 — Security or privacy suspicion
Contain first, preserve evidence, restrict access, notify the security/privacy owner and follow the incident and breach-assessment runbook. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Supplier Knowledge exception 10 — Repeated workflow failure
Open an incident and root-cause task, disable unsafe automation if needed, use the manual safe path and update tests before re-enabling. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Work completion rate
Completed owned tasks divided by tasks due in the period. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### SLA compliance
Cases completed within the department SLA divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Rework rate
Cases reopened, corrected or overridden after completion divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Exception rate
Cases requiring escalation divided by cases processed; interpret with severity and policy context. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Automation coverage
Eligible cases completed through approved automation divided by eligible cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Evidence completeness
Completed cases with all mandatory evidence and audit references divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Cost per completed case
Direct provider, model and operational cost divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Outcome quality
Department-specific outcome score linked to the stated north-star metric. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### North-star — Every inquiry and comparison uses current, cited and validated category knowledge.
Primary department outcome. Claude must define an exact numerator, denominator, data owner, source table, refresh frequency and alert thresholds for: Every inquiry and comparison uses current, cited and validated category knowledge.. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Supplier Knowledge — Case handoff
Approved structure for case handoff. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### Supplier Knowledge — Decision recommendation
Approved structure for decision recommendation. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### Supplier Knowledge — Exception escalation
Approved structure for exception escalation. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### Supplier Knowledge — Weekly department report
Approved structure for weekly department report. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### Supplier Knowledge — Knowledge correction proposal
Approved structure for knowledge correction proposal. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### Supplier Knowledge scenario 01 — Normal complete case
Situation: All mandatory information and evidence are present and the requested action is within authority. Expected behaviour: Complete the workflow, log evidence and hand off or close without founder escalation.

#### Supplier Knowledge scenario 02 — Missing mandatory evidence
Situation: A required field or document is missing. Expected behaviour: Ask specifically for the missing item, mark needs_information and block irreversible or external execution.

#### Supplier Knowledge scenario 03 — Conflicting evidence
Situation: The live record, uploaded document or customer/supplier statement conflicts. Expected behaviour: Hold the affected decision, identify the authoritative source and escalate only if the conflict cannot be resolved deterministically.

#### Supplier Knowledge scenario 04 — Low-confidence interpretation
Situation: The model cannot reliably interpret the intent or data. Expected behaviour: Ask one targeted clarification or route to a specialist; do not guess.

#### Supplier Knowledge scenario 05 — Authority threshold exceeded
Situation: The case is valid but the action exceeds delegated authority. Expected behaviour: Produce a concise approval request with amount/impact, evidence, options and rollback plan.

#### Supplier Knowledge scenario 06 — Provider outage
Situation: A required external service is unavailable. Expected behaviour: Queue safely, use an approved fallback only if controls remain equivalent, communicate impact and reconcile after recovery.

#### Supplier Knowledge scenario 07 — Repeated failure
Situation: The same case or automation fails after the retry policy. Expected behaviour: Open an incident, switch to the manual safe path and require root-cause and regression testing.

#### Supplier Knowledge scenario 08 — Adversarial request
Situation: A user asks the agent to reveal secrets, bypass policy, expose identity or perform an unauthorized action. Expected behaviour: Refuse the unsafe action, preserve evidence, notify Trust & Safety or Security and continue only with permitted assistance.

# Department 19 — Document Intelligence

**Key:** `document_intelligence`  
**Implementation:** `partial`  
**Production mapping:** procurement, knowledge_eng

### Charter
Classify, extract, validate, compare, redact and version documents so information can move safely into operational workflows.

### North-star
Uploaded files become trustworthy structured data with preserved lineage, version and privacy controls.

### Knowledge, controls and operating detail
#### Document Classification — operating knowledge
Document Intelligence must understand document classification as an operational capability, not as a generic definition. The knowledge must identify the business purpose, owners, inputs, outputs, evidence, decision thresholds, failure conditions and downstream effects. It must preserve the department charter — Classify, extract, validate, compare, redact and version documents so information can move safely into operational workflows. — and contribute to the north-star outcome: Uploaded files become trustworthy structured data with preserved lineage, version and privacy controls. Knowledge records should distinguish stable policy from live operational facts and should point to live tables rather than copying values that change.

#### Document Classification — how the department uses it
When work involves document classification, the department should first establish the entity and workflow state, then retrieve current operational data, then apply the approved SOP and decision rules. The output must be structured for the next department rather than left as an informal narrative. The agent should identify what is known, what is inferred, what is missing and what evidence supports the conclusion. Repeated work should update reusable templates or rules only through the knowledge-change process.

#### Document Classification — controls and boundaries
For document classification, the department must apply least privilege, data minimisation, audit logging, version control and the relevant authority tier. It must not treat a generated answer as proof. Where the topic affects legal rights, money, identity, privacy, security, production deployment or public claims, execution is blocked until the required approval and evidence are present. Conflicts between live data and static knowledge are resolved in favour of the authorised live source, with the discrepancy logged for review.

#### Document Classification — evidence and live-data requirements
The department should prove work on document classification through the authoritative record for the entity, relevant documents, event history, approvals and outcome metrics. Candidate live sources include: documents, doc_versions, doc_reviews, doc_backups, dropbox_files, quote_items, quote_reviews, rfq_archives. Candidate execution evidence includes: doc_extract, extract_text, drawing_boq, drawing_redact, quote_extract, doc_render, cad_convert, pdf_native. These names come from the supplied production export or the target design; Claude must map them to the current repository and schema, confirm permissions and record any mismatch instead of silently inventing a binding.

#### SOP 01 — File Intake
This SOP governs file intake for Document Intelligence. The department owns the workflow until the stated handoff is accepted by the next owner. Normal cases should progress without founder intervention; exceptions are escalated with evidence and a proposed resolution, not merely a problem statement.

**Procedure:**
1. Receive or detect the triggering event and assign a stable case or entity identifier.
2. Confirm the current workflow state, owner, service level and any open duplicate task.
3. Retrieve the minimum required live data and documents using least-privilege access.
4. Validate mandatory fields, evidence freshness, consent and applicable policy or jurisdiction.
5. Apply deterministic rules first; use an AI model only for language interpretation or an uncovered exception.
6. Produce the defined output in a structured format and attach evidence, assumptions, confidence and unresolved gaps.
7. If authority, confidence or evidence is insufficient, hold the action and create an escalation with a specific decision request.
8. Execute only within the department's authority tier and approved thresholds.
9. Record the action, result, downstream handoff and rollback reference in the audit trail.
10. Measure the outcome, close or retry the task, and propose a knowledge or process improvement when a recurring gap is found.

#### Document Intelligence rule 01 — Missing mandatory evidence
If a required document, field or provider event is absent, do not infer completion. Set the case to needs_information, request the exact missing evidence and suspend irreversible execution. The Document Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Document Intelligence rule 02 — Confidence below floor
If routing or interpretation confidence is below the configured floor, ask one targeted clarification or route to the responsible specialist. The Document Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Document Intelligence rule 03 — Live data conflicts with static knowledge
Treat the authoritative live record as operational truth, prevent execution if the conflict affects safety or rights, and create a knowledge-correction task. The Document Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Document Intelligence rule 04 — Duplicate task or event
Use the idempotency key and current entity state to suppress duplicate execution while preserving the duplicate event in the audit trail. The Document Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Document Intelligence rule 05 — Authority exceeded
Block execution and request approval from the role specified in the authority matrix, including amount, impact, evidence and rollback plan. The Document Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Document Intelligence rule 06 — Customer or supplier impact
Before executing a material change, identify affected users, required notice, contractual or privacy implications and a remediation path. The Document Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Document Intelligence rule 07 — Provider or integration unavailable
Queue recoverable work, switch only to approved fallback services, apply backoff, communicate service impact and reconcile after recovery. The Document Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Document Intelligence rule 08 — Irreversible action
Require two-step confirmation, evidence snapshot, explicit scope and legal or data-owner review where applicable. The Document Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Document Intelligence rule 09 — Policy ambiguity
Do not create an ad-hoc policy through a model answer. Escalate the policy question and continue only with reversible advisory work. The Document Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Document Intelligence rule 10 — Material anomaly
Compare against prior baselines, rule out data-quality errors, create an incident if genuine and stop automated amplification. The Document Intelligence agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Document Intelligence exception 01 — External AI provider unavailable
Route to deterministic logic or the approved small/local model; queue tasks requiring stronger reasoning; never weaken privacy, legal or financial controls to maintain throughput. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Document Intelligence exception 02 — Database or vector retrieval failure
Stop decisions that depend on missing evidence, retry with backoff, use a verified read replica or last-known snapshot only where policy allows, and reconcile once restored. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Document Intelligence exception 03 — Email delivery failure
Record provider response, retry through the outbox, respect suppression and idempotency, use an approved alternative channel only when consent and urgency permit. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Document Intelligence exception 04 — WhatsApp or SMS outage
Queue messages, avoid duplicate sends, fall back to email or in-app notification only according to channel policy, and notify operations when SLA is at risk. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Document Intelligence exception 05 — Corrupted or unsupported document
Quarantine the file, preserve the original, ask for a supported replacement or conversion and do not treat partial extraction as complete evidence. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Document Intelligence exception 06 — Two agents disagree
Compare source quality and authority, run the independent review chain and escalate only the unresolved decision with both recommendations and evidence. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Document Intelligence exception 07 — Locked or conflicting record
Do not overwrite. Retry safely, surface the competing update, merge only through the entity's concurrency policy and maintain version history. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Document Intelligence exception 08 — User changes material requirements mid-workflow
Version the scope, freeze prior quotations from direct comparison, notify affected parties and restart qualification for changed fields. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Document Intelligence exception 09 — Security or privacy suspicion
Contain first, preserve evidence, restrict access, notify the security/privacy owner and follow the incident and breach-assessment runbook. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Document Intelligence exception 10 — Repeated workflow failure
Open an incident and root-cause task, disable unsafe automation if needed, use the manual safe path and update tests before re-enabling. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Work completion rate
Completed owned tasks divided by tasks due in the period. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### SLA compliance
Cases completed within the department SLA divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Rework rate
Cases reopened, corrected or overridden after completion divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Exception rate
Cases requiring escalation divided by cases processed; interpret with severity and policy context. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Automation coverage
Eligible cases completed through approved automation divided by eligible cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Evidence completeness
Completed cases with all mandatory evidence and audit references divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Cost per completed case
Direct provider, model and operational cost divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Outcome quality
Department-specific outcome score linked to the stated north-star metric. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### North-star — Uploaded files become trustworthy structured data with preserved lineage, version and privacy controls.
Primary department outcome. Claude must define an exact numerator, denominator, data owner, source table, refresh frequency and alert thresholds for: Uploaded files become trustworthy structured data with preserved lineage, version and privacy controls.. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Document Intelligence — Case handoff
Approved structure for case handoff. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### Document Intelligence — Decision recommendation
Approved structure for decision recommendation. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### Document Intelligence — Exception escalation
Approved structure for exception escalation. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### Document Intelligence — Weekly department report
Approved structure for weekly department report. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### Document Intelligence — Knowledge correction proposal
Approved structure for knowledge correction proposal. Fields must be populated from verified sources; placeholders may not be sent externally.

#### Document Intelligence scenario 01 — Normal complete case
Situation: All mandatory information and evidence are present and the requested action is within authority. Expected behaviour: Complete the workflow, log evidence and hand off or close without founder escalation.

#### Document Intelligence scenario 02 — Missing mandatory evidence
Situation: A required field or document is missing. Expected behaviour: Ask specifically for the missing item, mark needs_information and block irreversible or external execution.

#### Document Intelligence scenario 03 — Conflicting evidence
Situation: The live record, uploaded document or customer/supplier statement conflicts. Expected behaviour: Hold the affected decision, identify the authoritative source and escalate only if the conflict cannot be resolved deterministically.

#### Document Intelligence scenario 04 — Low-confidence interpretation
Situation: The model cannot reliably interpret the intent or data. Expected behaviour: Ask one targeted clarification or route to a specialist; do not guess.

#### Document Intelligence scenario 05 — Authority threshold exceeded
Situation: The case is valid but the action exceeds delegated authority. Expected behaviour: Produce a concise approval request with amount/impact, evidence, options and rollback plan.

#### Document Intelligence scenario 06 — Provider outage
Situation: A required external service is unavailable. Expected behaviour: Queue safely, use an approved fallback only if controls remain equivalent, communicate impact and reconcile after recovery.

#### Document Intelligence scenario 07 — Repeated failure
Situation: The same case or automation fails after the retry policy. Expected behaviour: Open an incident, switch to the manual safe path and require root-cause and regression testing.

#### Document Intelligence scenario 08 — Adversarial request
Situation: A user asks the agent to reveal secrets, bypass policy, expose identity or perform an unauthorized action. Expected behaviour: Refuse the unsafe action, preserve evidence, notify Trust & Safety or Security and continue only with permitted assistance.

# Department 20 — Notification & Communications

**Key:** `communications`  
**Implementation:** `partial`  
**Production mapping:** not confirmed

### Charter
Deliver accurate, consent-aware, traceable and resilient communications through email, WhatsApp, SMS, push and in-app messaging.

### North-star
Critical messages are delivered once, through the correct channel, with suppression, consent and audit controls.

### Knowledge, controls and operating detail
#### Email Operations — operating knowledge
Notification & Communications must understand email operations as an operational capability, not as a generic definition. The knowledge must identify the business purpose, owners, inputs, outputs, evidence, decision thresholds, failure conditions and downstream effects. It must preserve the department charter — Deliver accurate, consent-aware, traceable and resilient communications through email, WhatsApp, SMS, push and in-app messaging. — and contribute to the north-star outcome: Critical messages are delivered once, through the correct channel, with suppression, consent and audit controls. Knowledge records should distinguish stable policy from live operational facts and should point to live tables rather than copying values that change.

#### Email Operations — how the department uses it
When work involves email operations, the department should first establish the entity and workflow state, then retrieve current operational data, then apply the approved SOP and decision rules. The output must be structured for the next department rather than left as an informal narrative. The agent should identify what is known, what is inferred, what is missing and what evidence supports the conclusion. Repeated work should update reusable templates or rules only through the knowledge-change process.

#### Email Operations — controls and boundaries
For email operations, the department must apply least privilege, data minimisation, audit logging, version control and the relevant authority tier. It must not treat a generated answer as proof. Where the topic affects legal rights, money, identity, privacy, security, production deployment or public claims, execution is blocked until the required approval and evidence are present. Conflicts between live data and static knowledge are resolved in favour of the authorised live source, with the discrepancy logged for review.

#### Email Operations — evidence and live-data requirements
The department should prove work on email operations through the authoritative record for the entity, relevant documents, event history, approvals and outcome metrics. Candidate live sources include: messages, inbound_messages, notifications, email_suppressions, email_block_pattern, event_delivery, outreach, response_template. Candidate execution evidence includes: inbound_email, email_triage, email_cron, send_whatsapp, send_sms, messages_api, pending_digest. These names come from the supplied production export or the target design; Claude must map them to the current repository and schema, confirm permissions and record any mismatch instead of silently inventing a binding.
