#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution rule 01 — Missing mandatory evidence
If a required document, field or provider event is absent, do not infer completion. Set the case to needs_information, request the exact missing evidence and suspend irreversible execution. The Strategy, Performance & Evolution agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution rule 02 — Confidence below floor
If routing or interpretation confidence is below the configured floor, ask one targeted clarification or route to the responsible specialist. The Strategy, Performance & Evolution agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution rule 03 — Live data conflicts with static knowledge
Treat the authoritative live record as operational truth, prevent execution if the conflict affects safety or rights, and create a knowledge-correction task. The Strategy, Performance & Evolution agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution rule 04 — Duplicate task or event
Use the idempotency key and current entity state to suppress duplicate execution while preserving the duplicate event in the audit trail. The Strategy, Performance & Evolution agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution rule 05 — Authority exceeded
Block execution and request approval from the role specified in the authority matrix, including amount, impact, evidence and rollback plan. The Strategy, Performance & Evolution agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution rule 06 — Customer or supplier impact
Before executing a material change, identify affected users, required notice, contractual or privacy implications and a remediation path. The Strategy, Performance & Evolution agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution rule 07 — Provider or integration unavailable
Queue recoverable work, switch only to approved fallback services, apply backoff, communicate service impact and reconcile after recovery. The Strategy, Performance & Evolution agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution rule 08 — Irreversible action
Require two-step confirmation, evidence snapshot, explicit scope and legal or data-owner review where applicable. The Strategy, Performance & Evolution agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution rule 09 — Policy ambiguity
Do not create an ad-hoc policy through a model answer. Escalate the policy question and continue only with reversible advisory work. The Strategy, Performance & Evolution agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution rule 10 — Material anomaly
Compare against prior baselines, rule out data-quality errors, create an incident if genuine and stop automated amplification. The Strategy, Performance & Evolution agent must record which rule fired, the relevant entity state and the downstream action.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution exception 01 — External AI provider unavailable
Route to deterministic logic or the approved small/local model; queue tasks requiring stronger reasoning; never weaken privacy, legal or financial controls to maintain throughput. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution exception 02 — Database or vector retrieval failure
Stop decisions that depend on missing evidence, retry with backoff, use a verified read replica or last-known snapshot only where policy allows, and reconcile once restored. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution exception 03 — Email delivery failure
Record provider response, retry through the outbox, respect suppression and idempotency, use an approved alternative channel only when consent and urgency permit. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution exception 04 — WhatsApp or SMS outage
Queue messages, avoid duplicate sends, fall back to email or in-app notification only according to channel policy, and notify operations when SLA is at risk. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution exception 05 — Corrupted or unsupported document
Quarantine the file, preserve the original, ask for a supported replacement or conversion and do not treat partial extraction as complete evidence. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution exception 06 — Two agents disagree
Compare source quality and authority, run the independent review chain and escalate only the unresolved decision with both recommendations and evidence. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution exception 07 — Locked or conflicting record
Do not overwrite. Retry safely, surface the competing update, merge only through the entity's concurrency policy and maintain version history. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution exception 08 — User changes material requirements mid-workflow
Version the scope, freeze prior quotations from direct comparison, notify affected parties and restart qualification for changed fields. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution exception 09 — Security or privacy suspicion
Contain first, preserve evidence, restrict access, notify the security/privacy owner and follow the incident and breach-assessment runbook. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution exception 10 — Repeated workflow failure
Open an incident and root-cause task, disable unsafe automation if needed, use the manual safe path and update tests before re-enabling. The department remains accountable for state, communication and reconciliation until the exception is formally handed off or closed.

#### Work completion rate
Completed owned tasks divided by tasks due in the period. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### SLA compliance
Cases completed within the department SLA divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Rework rate
Cases reopened, corrected or overridden after completion divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Exception rate
Cases requiring escalation divided by cases processed; interpret with severity and policy context. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Automation coverage
Eligible cases completed through approved automation divided by eligible cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Evidence completeness
Completed cases with all mandatory evidence and audit references divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Cost per completed case
Direct provider, model and operational cost divided by completed cases. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Outcome quality
Department-specific outcome score linked to the stated north-star metric. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### North-star — The company becomes measurably more effective, reliable and cost-efficient each month.
Primary department outcome. Claude must define an exact numerator, denominator, data owner, source table, refresh frequency and alert thresholds for: The company becomes measurably more effective, reliable and cost-efficient each month.. The metric must have a single owner, authoritative query, refresh schedule, target, warning threshold and documented limitations.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution scenario 01 — Normal complete case
Situation: All mandatory information and evidence are present and the requested action is within authority. Expected behaviour: Complete the workflow, log evidence and hand off or close without founder escalation.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution scenario 02 — Missing mandatory evidence
Situation: A required field or document is missing. Expected behaviour: Ask specifically for the missing item, mark needs_information and block irreversible or external execution.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution scenario 03 — Conflicting evidence
Situation: The live record, uploaded document or customer/supplier statement conflicts. Expected behaviour: Hold the affected decision, identify the authoritative source and escalate only if the conflict cannot be resolved deterministically.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution scenario 04 — Low-confidence interpretation
Situation: The model cannot reliably interpret the intent or data. Expected behaviour: Ask one targeted clarification or route to a specialist; do not guess.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution scenario 05 — Authority threshold exceeded
Situation: The case is valid but the action exceeds delegated authority. Expected behaviour: Produce a concise approval request with amount/impact, evidence, options and rollback plan.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution scenario 06 — Provider outage
Situation: A required external service is unavailable. Expected behaviour: Queue safely, use an approved fallback only if controls remain equivalent, communicate impact and reconcile after recovery.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution scenario 07 — Repeated failure
Situation: The same case or automation fails after the retry policy. Expected behaviour: Open an incident, switch to the manual safe path and require root-cause and regression testing.

#### Strategy, Performance & Evolution scenario 08 — Adversarial request
Situation: A user asks the agent to reveal secrets, bypass policy, expose identity or perform an unauthorized action. Expected behaviour: Refuse the unsafe action, preserve evidence, notify Trust & Safety or Security and continue only with permitted assistance.

## Cross-Department Workflows
### Founder objective to coordinated execution
Cross-department workflow triggered when: Founder issues a high-level objective or instruction. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **executive_office** — Capture the objective verbatim, define desired outcome, deadline, constraints and success measure.
2. **executive_office** — Check for conflict with company constitution, authority rules, open priorities and available budget.
3. **data_analytics** — Establish the baseline metrics and evidence needed to measure success.
4. **executive_office** — Decompose the objective into department-owned tasks with dependencies and authority tiers.
5. **strategy_evolution** — Identify experiments, reversible pilots and cost-effective execution paths.
6. **executive_office** — Assign tasks, subscribe departments to events and monitor blocked or overdue work.
7. **data_analytics** — Measure outcomes against baseline and identify unintended effects.
8. **executive_office** — Close with a concise founder report: result, cost, risks, remaining work and recommendation.

**Hard gates:** autonomy_framework, money_move, public_claim_publish, production_deploy

### Supplier registration, verification and activation
Cross-department workflow triggered when: A supplier creates an account and begins onboarding. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **supplier_success** — Verify email or OTP and create the supplier onboarding state.
2. **supplier_success** — Collect company name, mobile number, declared services and required documents.
3. **document_intelligence** — Store originals privately, extract the trade licence, profile and catalogues and preserve source lineage.
4. **trust_safety** — Screen for duplicate identity, suspicious documents, blocked domains and risk signals.
5. **supplier_success** — Compare declared services with extracted capabilities and map to operational categories.
6. **legal_compliance** — Confirm current agreement version and signed acceptance evidence.
7. **supplier_success** — Apply the automated licence/document gate; activate clean cases or request precise remediation.
8. **communications** — Send status, missing-document and activation messages through the approved channels.
9. **supplier_success** — Create document-completeness score and schedule renewal/expiry reminders.

**Hard gates:** supplier_enforcement, authentication_identity, legal_commitment

### Customer registration and immediate inquiry readiness
Cross-department workflow triggered when: A customer registers through the customer portal. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **customer_success** — Verify email or mobile OTP and create the customer profile.
2. **customer_success** — Collect name, mobile number, language and any minimum eligibility data.
3. **legal_compliance** — Present the current Terms and Privacy notices and record the accepted version.
4. **document_intelligence** — Generate and store acceptance evidence with time, IP and document hash where configured.
5. **trust_safety** — Check abuse, disposable-domain and duplicate-account risk without unnecessarily blocking legitimate access.
6. **customer_success** — Mark registration complete only when all backend gates pass.
7. **communications** — Send confirmation and route the customer directly to the inquiry flow.

**Hard gates:** authentication_identity, legal_commitment

### Customer inquiry to supplier-safe dispatch
Cross-department workflow triggered when: A verified customer starts or resumes an inquiry. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **rfq_intelligence** — Interpret ordinary customer language and create ranked category/subcategory candidates.
2. **rfq_intelligence** — Ask a targeted clarification if routing confidence is insufficient.
3. **supplier_knowledge** — Load only the applicable category questions, technical rules and quotation requirements from the supplier corpus.
4. **document_intelligence** — Extract attached files and map evidence to known inquiry fields.
5. **rfq_intelligence** — Ask missing mandatory and conditional questions in approved sequence.
6. **trust_safety** — Run inquiry legitimacy and abuse controls.
7. **document_intelligence** — Remove identity and contact details from supplier-visible text and files; fail closed on uncertainty.
8. **rfq_intelligence** — Build the immutable supplier-safe brief and calculate completeness/dispatch eligibility.
9. **marketplace_operations** — Match only eligible suppliers with the required capability, location and active status.
10. **communications** — Send the same supplier-safe scope to selected suppliers with response deadline and tracking.

**Hard gates:** destructive_data, authentication_identity

### Quotation collection, technical comparison and top-three recommendation
Cross-department workflow triggered when: One or more suppliers submit quotations for an inquiry. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **document_intelligence** — Preserve the original quotation and extract items, totals, taxes, terms, inclusions, exclusions and attachments.
2. **marketplace_operations** — Validate quote ownership, inquiry linkage, revision and deadline.
3. **supplier_knowledge** — Check each quotation against the structured inquiry, mandatory technical fields and category rules.
4. **marketplace_operations** — Normalize units, quantities, scope, commercial terms and explicit assumptions.
5. **supplier_knowledge** — Identify technical deviations, missing certificates, exclusions, approval risk and substitution requirements.
6. **data_analytics** — Calculate auditable scores using configured weights and the customer's stated priorities.
7. **marketplace_operations** — Rank all valid quotations and select the top three without hiding access to the remaining quotations.
8. **customer_success** — Generate an understandable English and Arabic comparison report that explains recommendation, trade-offs and unresolved risks.
9. **marketplace_operations** — Preserve all scores, rules, evidence and versioned report output for audit and challenge.

**Hard gates:** public_claim_publish, legal_commitment

### Chosen supplier reveal and payment
Cross-department workflow triggered when: Customer chooses a supplier and requests reveal. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **marketplace_operations** — Confirm that the selected quotation is current, belongs to the inquiry and has a valid reveal basis.
2. **payments_revenue** — Calculate the current configured reveal fee and applicable tax presentation.
3. **customer_success** — Show the exact amount and obtain deliberate confirmation.
4. **payments_revenue** — Create idempotent checkout and process the provider result.
5. **finance** — Record the transaction and accounting evidence without relying only on the client response.
6. **marketplace_operations** — Reveal only the chosen supplier after authoritative payment confirmation.
7. **communications** — Notify customer and supplier and record contact disclosure event.
8. **customer_success** — Start the non-response complaint window and support path.

**Hard gates:** money_move, authentication_identity, legal_commitment

### Supplier non-response complaint and refund review
Cross-department workflow triggered when: A customer complains that a revealed supplier is non-responsive. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **customer_success** — Validate complaint timing, selected supplier, reveal record and required written contact evidence.
2. **communications** — Attempt supplier contact through tracked approved channels.
3. **marketplace_operations** — Check supplier activity, message delivery and prior performance.
4. **trust_safety** — Assess repeated non-response or abuse pattern.
5. **customer_success** — Apply the current complaint policy and prepare the recommended remedy.
6. **payments_revenue** — Process any approved refund idempotently through the provider.
7. **finance** — Reconcile the refund and accounting entries.
8. **supplier_success** — Update supplier performance, coaching, suspension or enforcement case as appropriate.

**Hard gates:** money_move, supplier_enforcement, legal_commitment

### Expense email to financial reporting
Cross-department workflow triggered when: A receipt or invoice arrives at the approved expenses inbox or is uploaded. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **communications** — Authenticate and store the inbound message and attachments.
2. **document_intelligence** — Extract supplier, date, currency, subtotal, tax, total, invoice number and payment evidence.
3. **trust_safety** — Check duplicate, altered-document and suspicious-sender signals.
4. **finance** — Map to chart of accounts, tax treatment, department, project and approval requirement.
5. **finance** — Create or update the expense/AP record; do not post final entries when mandatory evidence is missing.
6. **finance** — Reconcile against payment or bank evidence when available.
7. **data_analytics** — Refresh burn, budget and forecast metrics.
8. **finance** — Include exceptions and optimisation recommendations in the scheduled management report.

**Hard gates:** money_move, legal_commitment

### Marketing content and campaign publication
Cross-department workflow triggered when: A content slot, campaign objective or founder instruction is due. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **marketing** — Translate the objective into audience, message, channel, format, CTA and success metric.
2. **supplier_knowledge** — Verify technical/category claims where the content describes products, services or requirements.
3. **legal_compliance** — Review new legal, privacy, comparative, price or performance claims.
4. **marketing** — Create platform-specific copy and creative using the approved brand system.
5. **data_analytics** — Confirm tracking, attribution and baseline metrics.
6. **marketing** — Submit public publishing or ad-spend actions through the required gate.
7. **communications** — Publish or schedule only to approved connected channels with deduplication.
8. **data_analytics** — Measure reach, qualified inquiries, conversion and cost; flag misleading or underperforming content.
9. **strategy_evolution** — Record lessons and propose controlled changes to the content system.

**Hard gates:** public_claim_publish, ad_spend, legal_commitment

### SEO research and website update
Cross-department workflow triggered when: Scheduled SEO review or approved content objective. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **data_analytics** — Identify search demand, ranking gaps and conversion opportunities using current evidence.
2. **supplier_knowledge** — Validate category terminology and factual trade content.
3. **marketing** — Create the content brief, page structure and approved claims.
4. **legal_compliance** — Review legal-page or regulated claims.
5. **engineering** — Implement or generate the page in staging with structured data and localization.
6. **qa_testing** — Check links, mobile layout, metadata, accessibility, Arabic rendering and factual consistency.
7. **engineering** — Deploy through the release gate and preserve rollback.
8. **data_analytics** — Monitor ranking, traffic, inquiries and quality after release.

**Hard gates:** production_deploy, public_claim_publish

### Personal-data rights request
Cross-department workflow triggered when: A data subject submits an access, correction, portability, objection or erasure request. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **customer_success** — Log the request and verify the requester through a proportionate, secure process.
2. **legal_compliance** — Classify the right requested, legal scope, exceptions and response deadline.
3. **it_cybersecurity** — Identify systems, processors, backups and access restrictions.
4. **document_intelligence** — Collect relevant records and preserve evidence of the search.
5. **engineering** — Execute approved export, correction, restriction or erasure through scoped tooling.
6. **legal_compliance** — Review completeness and any lawful retention obligations.
7. **communications** — Send the approved response securely.
8. **it_cybersecurity** — Record closure, residual backups and follow-up controls.

**Hard gates:** authentication_identity, destructive_data, legal_commitment

### Security or privacy incident response
Cross-department workflow triggered when: Monitoring, user report or provider alert indicates a potential security or privacy incident. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **it_cybersecurity** — Triage severity, contain access and preserve volatile evidence.
2. **engineering** — Disable affected feature, integration, credential or deployment path when required.
3. **trust_safety** — Identify affected accounts, transactions and abuse indicators.
4. **legal_compliance** — Assess legal, contractual and notification obligations.
5. **communications** — Prepare controlled internal and external communications; do not speculate.
6. **it_cybersecurity** — Eradicate the cause, recover services and rotate affected credentials.
7. **qa_testing** — Run security and regression tests before normal service resumes.
8. **executive_office** — Review material impact, decisions, cost and external reporting.
9. **strategy_evolution** — Track corrective actions and verify benefits.

**Hard gates:** secrets_security, authentication_identity, destructive_data, public_claim_publish, legal_commitment

### Software change and production release
Cross-department workflow triggered when: An approved product, compliance, security or operational change is ready. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **engineering** — Define change, affected components, data migration, dependencies and rollback.
2. **legal_compliance** — Review changes affecting terms, privacy, consumer rights, regulated claims or records.
3. **ai_model_ops** — Evaluate changes to prompts, agents, models, retrieval or authority.
4. **qa_testing** — Run unit, integration, regression, security, performance and business-scenario tests.
5. **it_cybersecurity** — Review access, secrets, observability and continuity impact.
6. **engineering** — Deploy to staging and capture evidence.
7. **engineering** — Request production approval with test results and rollback plan.
8. **engineering** — Deploy, monitor canaries and automatically stop or roll back on defined failure.
9. **qa_testing** — Perform post-release validation and close only after metrics stabilize.

**Hard gates:** production_deploy, secrets_security, autonomy_framework

### Knowledge acquisition, review and promotion
Cross-department workflow triggered when: A source changes, a gap is detected, an agent is corrected or new company policy is approved. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **knowledge_learning** — Create a change record with source, affected scopes, urgency and current validation status.
2. **supplier_knowledge** — For supplier-domain knowledge, map categories, subcategories, questions and decision rules.
3. **legal_compliance** — Review legal, tax, privacy and regulatory material; do not auto-promote.
4. **ai_model_ops** — Assess retrieval, prompt and model impact.
5. **qa_testing** — Run knowledge exams and scenario regressions.
6. **knowledge_learning** — Version records, preserve supersession and promote only approved content.
7. **data_analytics** — Monitor usage, answer quality, overrides and stale knowledge.
8. **knowledge_learning** — Schedule future review and notify affected agents.

**Hard gates:** legal_commitment, autonomy_framework

### Agent or employee onboarding and certification
Cross-department workflow triggered when: A new agent/employee role is created or a recertification becomes due. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **hr_people** — Define role, manager, responsibilities, skills, limits and performance metrics.
2. **it_cybersecurity** — Grant least-privilege identity, tools and data scope.
3. **knowledge_learning** — Assign company-core and department knowledge layers.
4. **ai_model_ops** — Configure model, prompt, tools, memory and confidence policy.
5. **qa_testing** — Run role-specific scenario and safety tests.
6. **hr_people** — Place the role in onboarding/probation until required scores are achieved.
7. **executive_office** — Approve high-authority roles and delegations.
8. **knowledge_learning** — Schedule review, decay and recertification.

**Hard gates:** authentication_identity, autonomy_framework

### External provider outage and continuity
Cross-department workflow triggered when: A critical AI, email, messaging, payment, storage or cloud provider is unavailable or degraded. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **it_cybersecurity** — Confirm outage scope, severity and provider status; create incident.
2. **engineering** — Stop unsafe retries and protect data consistency.
3. **ai_model_ops** — Route AI tasks to deterministic logic, cache or approved fallback tiers where safe.
4. **communications** — Queue messages and notify affected users only when material.
5. **payments_revenue** — Pause or reconcile payment actions that lack authoritative confirmation.
6. **engineering** — Restore using approved fallback or wait strategy and monitor recovery.
7. **data_analytics** — Measure backlog, SLA impact and cost.
8. **executive_office** — Review material business impact and vendor risk.
9. **strategy_evolution** — Update continuity plan and supplier strategy.

**Hard gates:** secrets_security, money_move, public_claim_publish

### Supplier suspension, ban and appeal
Cross-department workflow triggered when: Fraud, expired critical documents, repeated non-response, abuse or serious quality failure is detected. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **trust_safety** — Open a case with evidence, risk severity and immediate containment recommendation.
2. **supplier_success** — Review supplier history, documents, response and prior coaching.
3. **marketplace_operations** — Pause matching or dispatch where continued participation creates risk.
4. **legal_compliance** — Review agreement, notice, evidence and appeal requirements for serious action.
5. **supplier_success** — Apply temporary hold or request final approval according to authority.
6. **communications** — Send factual notice, remedy requirements and appeal route.
7. **trust_safety** — Review appeal independently and document outcome.
8. **supplier_success** — Restore, maintain restriction or offboard; update supplier score and knowledge.

**Hard gates:** supplier_enforcement, legal_commitment

### Monthly operating and financial review
Cross-department workflow triggered when: Monthly close and KPI cycle. The workflow must use explicit state, ownership and accepted handoffs; informal messages do not replace workflow state.

1. **finance** — Close and reconcile revenue, expenses, cash, obligations and provider costs.
2. **data_analytics** — Refresh department, marketplace, supplier, customer, marketing and AI metrics.
3. **all** — Submit department outcomes, risks, SLA issues, cost and next-month priorities.
4. **executive_office** — Resolve metric conflicts, assess objectives and identify decisions.
5. **strategy_evolution** — Identify cost, quality and organizational improvements.
6. **executive_office** — Publish the internal management report and approved founder brief.
7. **knowledge_learning** — Capture material lessons and policy changes.

**Hard gates:** money_move, autonomy_framework


## Runtime Governance
### Data classification — public
Information approved for public release, including published website and approved marketing content.

### Data classification — internal
Routine internal policies, SOPs, non-sensitive metrics and operational documentation.

### Data classification — confidential
Customer, supplier, financial, contract, unpublished strategy and detailed system information.

### Data classification — restricted_personal
Identity, contact details, KYC, signed evidence, payment references and personal-data requests.

### Data classification — restricted_security
Secrets, credentials, signing keys, vulnerability details and privileged configuration.

### Model route — deterministic_only
A validated rule, workflow state, calculation or database query fully determines the outcome.

### Model route — retrieval_plus_small_model
Natural language must be mapped to structured fields and the applicable internal knowledge is already available.

### Model route — premium_text_model
The text is materially ambiguous, multi-document, conflicting or requires advanced synthesis beyond the approved small-model quality threshold.

### Model route — multimodal_model
The task requires understanding images, drawings, scans or visually structured documents that deterministic extractors cannot handle.

### Model route — professional_review
The output could create binding legal, engineering, tax, medical, security or authority consequences.

### Memory policy — session_context
Temporary context for the active case. Include only data required for the current task; expire or summarise after closure.

### Memory policy — agent_memory
Role-specific corrections and preferences that are evidence-backed and non-sensitive. Promotion requires source and review.

### Memory policy — department_memory
Reusable departmental decisions, lessons, templates and exceptions. Must be versioned and visible to the owning department.

### Memory policy — institutional_memory
Company-wide outcomes and lessons that should survive personnel or model changes. Must reference evidence and outcome.

### Memory policy — live_data_not_memory
Current customer, supplier, inquiry, payment and task state is retrieved live and must not be frozen as memory.

### Memory policy — prohibited_memory
Secrets, credentials, full payment details, unnecessary identity data, unverified allegations and hidden model reasoning may not be stored as knowledge or memory.

### Audit requirement — business_action
Every workflow execution records actor, department, entity, state before/after, evidence, policy/rule, confidence, result and timestamp.

### Audit requirement — approval
Approvals record approver, scope, amount or impact, evidence reviewed, expiry and any conditions.

### Audit requirement — model_call
Model calls record task class, model route, provider/model identifier, input/output hashes where safe, cost, latency, confidence and fallback.

### Audit requirement — data_access
Restricted data access records user/agent, purpose, entity, fields or scope, timestamp and result.

### Audit requirement — security_event
Security events preserve severity, source, affected assets/accounts, containment, evidence and closure.

### Audit requirement — knowledge_change
Knowledge changes preserve previous version, source, reviewer, validation status, effective date and supersession.

### Audit requirement — financial_event
Financial events reconcile provider reference, internal transaction, invoice, accounting entries and reversal/refund.

### Audit requirement — public_publish
Public publishing records content version, approver, channels, time, campaign and correction history.

### Incident priority — P0 critical
Active security breach, widespread data exposure, unauthorised money movement, complete production outage or irreversible corruption.

### Incident priority — P1 high
Major customer/supplier workflow unavailable, payment or identity service materially impaired, high-risk privacy issue or repeated harmful automation.

### Incident priority — P2 medium
Degraded non-critical function, limited user impact, repeated SLA breach or important integration issue with workaround.

### Incident priority — P3 low
Minor defect, isolated content issue or enhancement with no material risk.
